name: pivot-invariants
of: a strategic asset that remains valuable across a total change in objective
why: to identify core strengths that survive radical shifts in market or theater
gate_why: Clear, distinct categories of foundational strategic assets (e.g., raw capital, compute, high-IQ talent) that transcend specific objectives.

name: negative-intent-signals
of: a somatic gesture that reliably indicates the absence of aggressive intent
why: to de-escalate high-tension physical encounters through precise body language
gate_why: Somatic gestures are highly specific and enumerable to well over 10 items (e.g., open palms, exposed neck, gaze aversion).

name: operational-dogmas
of: a rigid belief within an organization that limits its operational flexibility
why: to audit and remove cognitive bottlenecks in complex logistics
gate_why: Organizational dogmas are distinct, real categories of rigid beliefs (e.g., 'zero-defect culture', 'never outsource core') that can be easily enumerated.

name: coalition-frictions
of: a specific type of inefficiency unique to cooperative alliances
why: to calculate the true cost of partnership versus unilateral action
gate_why: Distinct types of alliance inefficiencies (e.g., intelligence compartmentalization, burden-shifting, command ambiguity) are real and enumerable.

name: deal-flow-reflexivities
of: a way in which the volume of opportunities alters the criteria for selection
why: to prevent quality degradation in high-velocity investment environments
gate_why: Mechanisms of reflexivity in high-volume environments (e.g., decision fatigue, shifting to proxy signals, threshold raising) are distinct and enumerable.

name: narrative-feedbacks
of: a mechanism where a propaganda narrative is validated by the target's reaction
why: to design influence operations that are self-reinforcing
gate_why: Clearly defined mechanisms (e.g., self-fulfilling prophecy, baiting overreaction) forming a genuine family of influence operations.

name: impasse-inventions
of: a synthetic bargaining chip created to break a deadlocked negotiation
why: to provide creative exits from zero-sum stalemates
gate_why: Synthetic bargaining chips (e.g., future conditional stakes, face-saving semantic redefinitions, third-party escrows) represent a clear, enumerable set of negotiation tools.

name: model-collapse-markers
of: an observable phenomenon indicating a total failure of an epistemic framework
why: to provide early warning for intelligence or analytical failure
gate_why: Observable phenomena of epistemic failure (e.g., reliance on epicycles, predictive inversion, institutional doubling-down) are robust and enumerable.

name: leverage-discoveries
of: a previously hidden point in a system where small inputs yield massive outputs
why: to map the geometry of power within complex bureaucracies
gate_why: Categories of systemic leverage points (e.g., feedback loops, information flows, rules, buffers) are famously enumerable (e.g., Meadows' 12 leverage points).

name: somatic-atoms
of: an irreducible unit of body language that cannot be further decomposed
why: to build a periodic table of non-verbal communication for deception detection
gate_why: Irreducible units of body language are scientifically established and enumerable (e.g., Ekman's Facial Action Coding System has 46 action units).

name: decision-tree-topologies
of: a specific shape or structure of logic in a complex decision path
why: to classify the 'terrain' of abstract strategic problems
gate_why: Structural topologies of logic or decision paths (e.g., linear chain, binary fan-out, converging, bottleneck, cyclic) form a clear, enumerable set.

name: preemption-archtypes
of: a psychological root cause for the urge to strike first
why: to diagnose and mitigate the biological drive toward preemptive war
gate_why: Psychological root causes for preemptive strikes (e.g., fear of loss, zero-sum framing, resource paranoia, honor defense) are distinct and enumerable.

name: cooperative-masks
of: a simulated helpful behavior used to hide a competitive or predatory intent
why: to detect 'wolves in sheep's clothing' in diplomatic or business settings
gate_why: Simulated helpful behaviors (e.g., malicious compliance, concern trolling, usurping control via 'assistance') form a robust and observable category list.

name: discourse-terminators
of: an argument that renders all further debate on a topic impossible
why: to identify cognitive 'black holes' in political or social discourse
gate_why: Thought-terminating arguments (e.g., Godwin's law, appeal to subjective unassailability, shifting the burden of proof to impossibility) are highly enumerable.

name: exchange-ontologies
of: a fundamental category of value exchanged in non-monetary deals
why: to broaden the scope of what can be negotiated in complex trades
gate_why: Fundamental categories of non-monetary value (e.g., status, access, time, protection, legitimacy, forgiveness) are distinct and clearly enumerable.

name: negotiator-check-loops
of: an internal mental check used to maintain composure during high-stakes deals
why: to systematize the training of emotional resilience in diplomats
gate_why: Internal mental checks (e.g., tactile grounding, tactical breathing, labeling emotions, BATNA reviews) are distinct cognitive/behavioral techniques.

name: velocity-bottlenecks
of: a constraint that only appears when an operation exceeds a certain speed
why: to prevent 'systemic shatter' during rapid scaling or blitzkrieg
gate_why: Speed-induced constraints (e.g., communication lag, thermal dissipation, decision fatigue, supply line stretching) are clear, enumerable physical and systemic phenomena.

name: ghost-leverages
of: an obsolete source of power that still influences behavior through habit
why: to identify where influence is being exerted by phantom authorities
gate_why: Obsolete sources of influence (e.g., deprecated titles, legacy software defaults, former infrastructure, historical precedent) are a distinct, real family.

name: risk-rebound-effects
of: a mitigation strategy that creates a new risk larger than the original
why: to avoid 'cobra effects' in safety engineering and finance
gate_why: Mitigation strategies that backfire (Cobra effect, Jevons paradox, over-prescription of antibiotics, suppressing minor forest fires) form a well-known, enumerable family.

name: hardening-vulnerabilities
of: a weakness created specifically by the process of securing a system
why: to find the 'chink in the armor' of highly protected targets
gate_why: Security-induced vulnerabilities (e.g., single point of failure via key centralization, reduced usability creating workarounds, encryption overhead) are an enumerable, well-studied family.

name: universal-susceptibilities
of: a cross-cultural constant in how humans respond to persuasion
why: to identify the 'hard-wired' targets for global influence operations
gate_why: Cross-cultural constants in persuasion (e.g., reciprocity, social proof, authority, scarcity, in-group bias) are distinct, proven, and highly enumerable.
